title: Implementing Cloud Security Monitoring with AWS CloudWatch and Prometheus
objectives: Configure AWS CloudWatch to monitor cloud resources for security threats
Set up Prometheus to collect metrics from cloud services
Integrate CloudWatch with Prometheus for real-time anomaly detection
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of AWS CloudFormation and IAM roles
Understanding of Prometheus configuration and query language
Familiarity with Linux shell scripting and command-line tools

mission_brief.briefing: Your mission, should you choose to accept it, is to monitor and detect security threats on our cloud infrastructure.
rules_of_engagement: You must implement AWS CloudWatch alarms for CPU usage above 70% on all EC2 instances
You must configure Prometheus to collect metrics from the RDS database instance
You must integrate CloudWatch with Prometheus to trigger alerts when threshold values are exceeded

content.concept: Cloud security monitoring is a critical aspect of maintaining the integrity and confidentiality of cloud-based resources. AWS CloudWatch provides real-time monitoring and logging capabilities, while Prometheus collects metrics from various services. By integrating these tools, we can identify potential security threats and respond promptly.
content.walkthrough: To implement cloud security monitoring with AWS CloudWatch and Prometheus, we'll first configure CloudWatch to monitor EC2 instances for CPU usage above 70%. Then, we'll set up Prometheus to collect metrics from the RDS database instance. Finally, we'll integrate CloudWatch with Prometheus to trigger alerts when threshold values are exceeded.
checkpoints: Verify that AWS CloudWatch alarms are triggered for CPU usage above 70% on all EC2 instances
Check that Prometheus is collecting metrics from the RDS database instance
Confirm that alerts are triggered in real-time when threshold values are exceeded
common_mistakes: Failing to configure IAM roles correctly for AWS CloudWatch and Prometheus integration
Incorrectly setting up alert thresholds in CloudWatch and Prometheus
Neglecting to validate metrics collection from various services

lab.setup:
# Install necessary packages on the EC2 instance
sudo yum install -y awscli
# Configure AWS CLI credentials for CloudWatch access
aws configure set aws_access_key_id YOUR_ACCESS_KEY_ID
aws configure set aws_secret_access_key YOUR_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
steps:
# Create an IAM role for AWS CloudWatch to monitor EC2 instances
aws iam create-role --role-name cloudwatch-monitoring --description "Role for AWS CloudWatch monitoring"

# Attach necessary policies to the IAM role
aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name cloudwatch-monitoring --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/CloudWatchAgentServerlessRole

# Configure Prometheus to collect metrics from RDS database instance
sudo yum install -y epel-release
sudo amazon-linux-extras enable prometheus
sudo rpm -Uvh https://s3.amazonaws.com/prometheus-kubernetes/latest/prometheus-node-exporter-0.16.0.x86_64.rpm

# Integrate CloudWatch with Prometheus to trigger alerts when threshold values are exceeded
aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm --alarm-name cpu-high-alert --metric-name CPUUtilization --namespace AWS/EC2 --statistic Average --period 300 --threshold 70

# Verify that alerts are triggered in real-time when threshold values are exceeded
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/EC2 --metric-name CPUUtilization --dimension Name=InstanceId,i-12345678 --statistics Average
safety: Be cautious when creating IAM roles and attaching policies to prevent unauthorized access.
Monitor CPU usage and memory consumption on EC2 instances to avoid overloading the system.
Regularly update Prometheus and CloudWatch packages to ensure security patches are applied.

bug_injection.description: A critical vulnerability in an EC2 instance is causing CPU usage to exceed 90%.
bug_injection.bad_state:
# Simulate the critical vulnerability by modifying the EC2 instance configuration
aws ec2 modify-instance-attribute --instance-id i-12345678 --attribute InstanceType --value t2.micro

interrogation_questions: What are the primary differences between CloudWatch and Prometheus in terms of functionality?
How would you troubleshoot a situation where alerts are not triggering correctly?
Explain the concept of "least privilege" in relation to IAM roles and policies.
